admission.claim_boundary: Closed initial inventory only. This block states which local path packages may resolve, for which exact target profiles, with which exact feature sets, under whose ownership and decision. It is not a donor audit: no FrankenSuite or Asupersync package is admitted and `foundation_admissions` remains empty.

packet_completion.reason: FA-053 and FA-054 are general packets: a freeze of the complete transitive dependency policy, and a general Cargo admission compiler. What exists here qualifies only the closed initial inventory: two local path packages, no external admission path, and one target profile per actually collected metadata. Qualifying the initial inventory does not close either packet, and neither packet may be marked complete on the strength of this block or its checker.
still_required: Per-target source, feature, build-script and runtime/downloaded-artifact inventories for every foundation considered for admission.
A reachable external admission path with a positive case, which does not exist today.
A lockfile-derived (package, source, checksum) mapping, which is a precondition of that path rather than an addition to this one.
A target profile for every target the product claims, each backed by actually collected metadata.

external_admission.reason: Cargo metadata cannot establish a package checksum, what a build script does when executed, or what bytes a loader downloads at run time. Admitting an external package on metadata evidence would be admission on absent evidence. The checker therefore refuses every external package unconditionally, and refuses any policy that carries an external row, so that no boolean or attestation field can stand in for an inspection that has not happened.

required_fields_when_implemented.note: The owned contract checker requires every listed identity, scope, closure and governance field name as future rule data. It does not accept external rows: every external package remains refused regardless of fields, flags or attestations. A complete source/build/runtime review is still required before a future implementation may support external admission.

external_admission.unblocked_by: Full per-target source, feature, build-script and runtime/downloaded-artifact inspection, which FA-053 defers and which no field in this file can substitute for.

identity_rules.local_package_identity: name + version + manifest_path relative to the metadata document's own workspace_root, compared by path components
identity_rules.external_package_identity: name + version + the exact opaque source string, compared verbatim (external is refused regardless)
identity_rules.path_containment: manifest_path must be absolute, free of `.` and `..`, and contained in workspace_root by path components. A byte-prefix comparison would accept a sibling directory such as `/workspacextask` under root `/workspace`.
identity_rules.decision_semantics: Every row carries an explicit owner and an explicit decision. Only the exact decision value `admitted` admits; any other value, including a pending or provisional one, refuses. A row without an owner or a decision is a policy load error, because an unowned or undecided row is not an admission.

target_profiles.evidence: Actual rustup run nightly-2026-08-31 cargo metadata --format-version 1 --locked --offline --filter-platform aarch64-apple-darwin, exit 0, operator host 2026-09-07. artifacts/execution/2026-09-07-apple-metadata-rustup.json; failed direct-cargo toolchain syntax attempt retained separately. Every gate recollects this target; collection is not compilation or runtime qualification.
Actual named-target metadata collected through RCH on hz4, exit 0, 2026-09-07. artifacts/execution/2026-09-07-linux-metadata-rch-job.log and .json. Every gate recollects the named profile.

target_profile_rules.collection_required: The gate collects cargo metadata with each exact --filter-platform target at execution time. A profile describes the expected graph; metadata collection may run on another host and is not target compilation or runtime qualification.

admission.rule_semantics: Each prohibition must be present and explicitly false. The checker refuses a policy that omits one, that sets one to true, or that sets one to a non-boolean. A policy file cannot switch off a constitutional prohibition, and a defaulted value is not an assertion.

metadata_invocation.why_locked_and_offline: cargo metadata without --locked may rewrite Cargo.lock, which would trip the exact lockfile guard from inside the gate that enforces it. --offline additionally prevents a network fetch during a check.
metadata_invocation.why_not_no_deps: --no-deps omits the resolve section entirely. docs/DEPENDENCY_CONSTITUTION.md forbids treating it as a transitive audit, so metadata whose resolve is null is refused rather than read as an empty passing graph.
metadata_invocation.why_filter_platform: A dependency can be activated only on one target. Without --filter-platform the document is not a per-target graph. Cargo metadata does not record which platform filter produced it, so the target is an explicit input to the checker and the report states that the binding rests on the invocation, not on the document.

not_established_by_this_checker: What a build script would do when executed.
What bytes a loader or model runtime would download at run time.
Whether an admitted upstream package contains unsafe code.
That the metadata was in fact produced with the declared --filter-platform target.
That any target other than a listed profile is admissible.
That the toolchain, std or operating system are themselves trustworthy.
admission.local_closure_boundary: Source review describes the enumerated local Rust code; actual snapshot bytes must match before admission. Build edges and target feature sets are independently checked against newly collected Cargo metadata. Operator binaries, std, toolchain and OS are explicit trust boundaries; this is not runtime attestation or foundation admission.

operator_qualification.boundary: Compiler-reported identity, checked against the prior qualified operator run; not binary authentication, Apple execution, or a complete release toolchain closure.
